clips.text: Have you ever looked at music and wondered what all those lines and dots actually mean? Let's find out!
Today we are going to learn some musical names.
Music is written on five lines like this.
Count them with me!
One.
Two.
Three.
Four.
Five.
Five lines together are called a stave.
This swirly symbol next to me is called a clef. It tells us how high or low to play.
This one is called the treble clef, and it is used for higher sounds!
And this clef looks totally different. Two dots and a curl. That's the bass clef, for lower sounds!
This little blob with a stick is called a note. It sits on the stave to show us which sound to play.
A note can sit on a line, like this one,
or in the gap between two lines, which we call a space.
Sometimes a note is too high or too low to fit on the stave.
We give it a tiny extra line to stand on. A ledger line.
Let's say them one more time:
